problem: The Go service showed latency spikes every few minutes, attributed to garbage collection of evicted cache entries.
title: Discord rewrites its Read States service from Go to Rust
context: Read States tracks which channels and messages each user has read, and is accessed on every connection, message and read.
decision_made: Rewrite the service in Rust, which frees memory as soon as entries are no longer used.
action_taken: Published an engineering post in February 2020 explaining the change.
observed_outcome: Discord reported the Rust version removed the periodic latency spikes. Secondary sources cite specific millisecond-to-microsecond improvements that were not confirmed against the original post.
lessons: For services with strict latency needs and large caches, garbage collection pauses can dominate tail latency.
limitations: Specific numbers were not verified. The result applies to one service with a particular access pattern, and rewriting has its own costs.

claims.claim_text: Discord rewrote its Read States service from Go to Rust.
A summary of the post said the Go version's latency spiked every few minutes because of garbage collection and that Rust frees memory immediately.
